M1_rail_height.question: rail height with/without the '#DsHeader' margin-bottom rule, and the DsVerb line box
M1_rail_height.blocks: CRIT.md ranked #11, and A2's airy -13 which stood until measured
M1_rail_height.line_note: the crit cites qss.py:344-346; at HEAD (716059a3) the three rules live at python/synapse/panel/designsystem/qss.py:375-377 (base + [density=airy] + [density=tight]). Same three rules, renumbered by the type/hue wave. The DsVerb margin rules are at :370-372.
M1_rail_height.method: compose SynapsePanel per profile at 340x760, read DsHeader height/sizeHint and the y/height of every visible direct sibling; then strip all three 'QWidget#DsHeader { ... margin-bottom ... }' rules from the stylesheet that carries them, unpolish/polish every widget, processEvents, re-read the same numbers. 3 rules removed in every profile.

gap_between_rail_and_next_section_px.with_and_without_the_rule: 0 in all six readings - DsSection.y() equals DsHeader.height() every time

content_box_px.derivation: height - 2 * margin; identical 20 at every density

M1_rail_height.verdict: Two findings, one of them against the crit. (1) The #DsHeader margin-bottom rule buys NO air: in all six readings the next sibling's y equals the rail's height exactly, so the rule never opens a gap between the rail and the section below it. SPACE's round-2 self-correction ('DsHeader margin no-op') is confirmed as far as air is concerned. (2) But it is not inert - it perturbs the rail's own allotted height, and the sign is INCONSISTENT across densities: airy -8 (rail squeezed 8px below its own 134 sizeHint), standard 0 (exactly the hint), tight +4 (rail stretched 4px past its 98 hint). A rule that shrinks the airy rail and grows the tight one is doing the opposite of what the density lever intends, in both directions. #11's premise - that the rule is spendable - holds; its stated direction does not, because deleting it makes the airy rail TALLER by 8, not shorter. (3) The DsVerb line box is 20px of content at every density, wrapped in 2 x gap(SPACE_SM) of QSS margin (12/8/6). A min-height of 26 would give the 20px box 6px of breathing room and remove 44->26 / 36->26 / 32->26, i.e. -18 / -10 / -6 per verb. A2's derived 'airy -13' is not reproduced by any single reading here; the measured airy figures are -18 per verb from the min-height swap and +8 from deleting the header rule. The chair owns reconciling which total the -13 was summing over - it is not the per-verb number and it is not the rail number.

M2_rail_verb_width.question: 'Bridge' / 'Start bridge' width vs row-2 slack post-F1
M2_rail_verb_width.verdict: 'Bridge' BUYS 8.65px of row-2 width rather than costing any - the rename is free and then some. 'Start bridge' costs +43.25px, which D2's GUTTER 30->24 remedy (-12) cannot cover; the crit derived ~+41 and the sign and magnitude both hold. USE's withdrawal of 'Start bridge' on width grounds is confirmed by measurement, not just by derivation.

qt_model._correction: CORRECTED 2026-09-15 by adversarial audit. The 'with_tracking' figures below were ARITHMETIC, not measurement: em x font-pixel-size over n-1 gaps, which is the CSS letter-spacing model. Qt does not do that. fontload.py:187 calls setLetterSpacing(PercentageSpacing, 115), which scales each advance by 1.15 and applies to EVERY cell, not n-1 gaps. Only 'advance' was measured; everything derived from it was modelled with the wrong model.
qt_model.verdict: The DIRECTION survives and the argument is unchanged: 'Bridge' still buys width, 'Start bridge' still costs far more than GUTTER 30->24 (-12) can cover. The magnitudes move: -8.05 not -8.65, and +40.25 not +43.25. Note the crit's own derived '~+41' matches the Qt model BETTER than this record's first figure did - the derivation was closer to the truth than the measurement that claimed to replace it.

M4_turn_beat_collapse.question: rendered collapse of the 24+16 / 8+12 turn-beat sum - does Qt SUM or COLLAPSE?
M4_turn_beat_collapse.blocks: CRIT.md ranked #3 (one owner for the turn beat)
M4_turn_beat_collapse.method: compose the panel at profile expert (standard density), append two YOU turns and two SYNAPSE turns through ChatDisplay's own append_user_message / append_synapse_message, then walk every QTextBlock reading blockFormat().topMargin()/bottomMargin() and documentLayout().blockBoundingRect() y/h. 26 blocks in the resulting document.
M4_turn_beat_collapse.verdict: NEITHER. The question 'sum or collapse' has no answer because the two numbers never meet. `bf.setTopMargin()` at chat_display.py:190-191 writes the SAME QTextBlockFormat property that the formatter's HTML margin-top produced, on the same block, after it - so it OVERWRITES. Measured: every 'group' block renders topMargin 16.0 (ROLE_GAPS.group at standard) and every 'row' block 12.0 (ROLE_GAPS.row), and the values 24 and 8 appear NOWHERE in the 26-block document, in any margin, on any block. message_formatter._GROUP_MARGIN_Y and _MSG_MARGIN_Y are dead for exactly the blocks that carry a role - which is the first block of every message, i.e. every block the turn beat is about. This is stronger than #3's claim: the crit argued there are two owners and the rendered beat is ambiguous; the measurement says there is already exactly one owner (chat_display), and the other one's constants - carefully reasoned in a 15-line comment at message_formatter.py:60-69 about 'the air BETWEEN turns' - are silently discarded. #3 ships as a deletion of the dead constants plus a comment correction, not as a spacing retune: the rendered beat does not change.

M5_transcript_body_x.question: transcript body x with document margin 0 vs the default 4
M5_transcript_body_x.method: same composed panel; set document().setDocumentMargin(0) vs leaving the Qt default 4, then read the first text block's absolute x as blockBoundingRect().x() + blockFormat().leftMargin() + layout().lineAt(0).x(), mapped into panel coordinates through viewport().mapTo(panel).
M5_transcript_body_x.verdict: #10's number is exact. setDocumentMargin(0) moves the transcript body from x=50 to x=46 in panel coordinates, and 46 = GUTTER 30 (the viewport's own x) + the formatter's 16px speaker indent - a content edge that is the sum of two named things instead of two named things plus Qt's unnamed 4. The document also loses 8px of height (4 top + 4 bottom), which is free vertical space in the transcript. Nothing else moved: the only delta anywhere in the two readings is the uniform -4 on x. '#10 one content edge at 46' is measured, not derived.

M6_bucket_count.question: boot-face chroma bucket count, against the CURRENT TEXT_ON_ACCENT
M6_bucket_count.blocks: CRIT.md ranked #4, and whether B1 is argued on principle or under a red pin
M6_bucket_count.TEXT_ON_ACCENT_provenance: python/synapse/panel/designsystem/tokens.py:206 at HEAD 716059a3 - i.e. AFTER the type and hue wave (#99/#100) merged. It is unchanged by that wave; #4 proposes to neutralise it and has NOT shipped.

TEXT_ON_ACCENT_arithmetic.note: 28 clears the >24 chroma predicate by 4. It is a chromatic ink by the instrument's own definition.

measured_live_boot_face.instrument: the pin's own _hue_buckets (tests/panel/test_bc_wave.py:269-282) run on widget.grab() of the composed panel at 340x760
measured_live_boot_face.legend: bucket -> number of distinct chromatic colours in that bucket. 0 = WARM mark, 2 = Doctor yellow, 13 = TEXT_ON_ACCENT ink and its antialias ramp, 14 = SIGNAL / SIGNAL_DEEP.

counterfactual_TEXT_ON_ACCENT_neutral.stand_in_caveat: #4 names no replacement value, so a chroma-0 near-black was substituted. Any achromatic ink gives the same bucket arithmetic.
counterfactual_TEXT_ON_ACCENT_neutral.how: patched on the tokens module in a FRESH hython process BEFORE qss was ever imported, so the generated stylesheet carries no #0F1F2B (verified: 'sheet_mentions_old_ink' == false). An in-process reload after the panel was built did NOT take - the first attempt showed no change and was discarded rather than reported.

M6_bucket_count.verdict: The boot face holds FOUR buckets today, in all three profiles - so `test_bc_wave.py:329` (`assert len(rest) <= 3`) is RED at HEAD, and B1 is currently being argued under a red pin. And #4 does not clear it. Neutralising TEXT_ON_ACCENT strips 57 of bucket 13's 59 colours, but TWO survive - (65,79,92) and (71,87,102), which are antialias pixels on the SIGNAL fill's own edge, landing at hue 205-206 and falling into bucket 13 rather than SIGNAL's 14. One pixel pair on the wrong side of a 15-degree boundary keeps the bucket alive and the count at 4. So: the fourth bucket is not a fourth hue family, it is the instrument's bucket boundary cutting through one accent's antialias ramp. That is exactly what B1 option (1) ('count tokens not buckets') said was happening, and it is now measured rather than suspected. CRIT.md:179 - 'After #4 the boot face sits at 3 buckets with Doctor included' - is REFUTED as written: it sits at 4 before #4 and at 4 after. B1 cannot be argued free of a red pin on this evidence; either the pin re-baselines to <= 4, or the predicate changes to count token families instead of 15-degree buckets.

M7_mono_weight_500.question: what mono weight 500 renders as today
M7_mono_weight_500.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE by this method. The crit's original reasoning (>=600 maps to setBold, so 500 is not a face the family ships) is neither confirmed nor refuted here, and stands as the better-supported reading.
M7_mono_weight_500._correction: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-15 by adversarial audit. This entry claimed 'weight 500 renders BOLD' and it is not supported by the instrument used. QFontInfo::bold() is DEFINED as weight() > Normal(400) - so 'bold=true at 500' merely restates 500 > 400 and says nothing about which face renders. The same reading returned exact_match: true with resolved_weight == requested at 400/500/600/700, which is impossible for a family shipping only two faces (Regular 400, Bold 700): QFontInfo was echoing the request. The repo's own mapping (fontload.py) never calls setBold below 600, which supports the crit's ORIGINAL reasoning that the threshold is >=600. The claim that this measurement overturned a derivation is withdrawn. Answering it properly needs the resolved font FILE (QRawFont) or fontload's mapping, not QFontInfo.
